suspended_reason: The cause is a parent-of-origin (imprinting) defect of the 11p15.5 imprinted region -- NOT a single-gene promoter switch. 11p15.5 carries two differentially methylated imprinting control regions: IC1 (H19/IGF2, controlling the paternally-expressed growth promoter IGF2 and the maternally-expressed lncRNA H19) and IC2 (KCNQ1OT1/CDKN1C, controlling the maternally-expressed growth-suppressor CDKN1C via the paternally-expressed antisense lncRNA KCNQ1OT1). Beckwith-Wiedemann arises from an EPIGENETIC/STRUCTURAL state across this locus: loss of methylation at IC2 (~50%), gain of methylation at IC1 (~5-10%), paternal uniparental disomy of 11p15.5 (~20%), or a maternal CDKN1C loss-of-function point mutation (~5%, ~40% of familial cases). The net effect -- increased IGF2 dosage and/or reduced CDKN1C -- is an overgrowth phenotype (macrosomia, macroglossia, abdominal-wall defects, hemihyperplasia, embryonal-tumour risk), but it is DEFINED by the parent-of-origin methylation/dosage state of an imprinted multi-gene region, so there is no analyzable single-gene gamma shift to read. Even the CDKN1C point-mutation minority is a parent-of-origin-dependent lesion (pathogenic only on the maternal allele) that a strand-symmetric promoter switch cannot capture. Held per the author's rule (no analyzable single-gene DNA -> hold). This is a THIRD imprinting hold, and the FIRST on a locus OTHER than 15q11-q13: where Prader-Willi (paternal loss) and Angelman (maternal UBE3A loss) are the reciprocal 15q11-q13 pair, Beckwith-Wiedemann is an 11p15.5 imprinting disorder on a DIFFERENT chromosome -- so the kit now demonstrates that the suspension rule keys on the LESION MECHANISM (imprinting) and GENERALISES across imprinted loci, not just within 15q. A parent-of-origin (epigenetic) multi-gene dosage model is future work, not a single-switch emergence.
discipline: no analyzable single-gene DNA read -> held (author's rule). Disclosed, not dropped.
